newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Zaitun says shares up on Islamic rumours.
newsitem.headline: Zaitun says shares up on Islamic rumours.

text.p: Malaysian cosmetics maker Zaitun Bhd said on Wednesday the surge in its share price could have been sparked off by Islamic institutional investors looking to invest in religiously-acceptable stocks.

"There has been rumours... that Zaitun's counter, being an Islamic, or 'Halal' counter, is much sought upon by Islamic institutional bodies which is only allowed to invest in Halal counters," said Zaitun in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The exchange had earlier placed restrictions on the trading of Zaitun stock after it leaped five ringgit to close at 12.50 ringgit.

'Halal' stocks are those that do not engage in practices contrary to the Moslem faith. Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd would be an example of such a stock as the bank does not offer interest-bearing accounts.
The stock made its debut on the exchange on June 13.
